description:

- reviews recent trends and changes to planning policy and legislation;\r
- includes a review of the Borough's town centres;\r
- identifies the need for retail uses;\r
- identifies the need for leisure uses;\r
- set outs out the implications for planning policy resulting from the analysis and provides recommendations on a strategy to accommodate future growth.

description:
The Authority is seeking to appoint a provider for the provision of Mental Health Supported Housing and Floating Support services for adults to provide person-centred tailored support for people with low level mental health conditions in the Royal Borough of Kingston.\r
\r

\r

\r
The award of contract will be subject to the preferred bidder entering into a housing management agreement with PA housing who own the properties.\r

title: Achieving for Children -  Joint Advocacy and Independent Visitor Service
description:
Achieving for Children is seeking to appoint a provider or providers working in partnership for the delivery of a Joint Advocacy and Independent Visitor Services across Operational Area 1 (London Borough of Kingston and Richmond) and Operational 2 (Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead).\r
\r
In order to fulfil its statutory Corporate Parenting responsibilities, AfC is seeking to appoint a provider to deliver and manage Children's Advocacy and Independent Visitor services for its children and young people aged 8-25. These include Children in Need; Children with a Child Protection Plan (CPP);  and Children Looked After (CLA); Care Leavers; Young people up to age of 25 with disabilities.\r
\r
The advocacy service will provide representation and support to children and young people aged 8-25( where there is an assessed disability need) to enable them make informed choices and decisions about services they receive which impact on their health and wellbeing. \r
\r
The independent visitor service will provide mentoring and befriending support for children and young people in care  who require help in enhancing their social connections, building trusting relationships\r
\r
Achieving for Children is using an Open Procedure for this procurement of services categorised as 'social and other specific services' under Schedule 3 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 ('PCR 2015'). This procurement exercise will therefore be subject to the Light Touch Regime ('LTR') under Regulations 74 to 77 as set out in the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.\r
\r
The initial contract period is for 36 months (3 years) from 1st June 2024 - 31st \r
May 2027,  with an option to extend for 2 (two) further periods of up to 12 months.  The overall contract term is therefore for 60 months (5 years). \r

The consultant shall be a suitably qualified and competent property consultant and registered to The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.

The Scope of Service that is required is expressly listed in the RICS Schedule of Services appended to this enquiry.

The Council agreed on the 22nd November 2022 to progress the redevelopment of the former care home, Murray House, on Acre Road from RIBA stage 1 and Outline Business Case through RIBA stages 2-3, leading up to the preparation of a planning application and production of a full business case.

The full Treasury Green Book 5 Case business case will be developed in tandem with a detailed planning application. The business case will request approval from the Council to ratify the detailed design proposal, confirm the procurement strategy, approve the project team to submit the planning application and allocate funding for the next stage of the project. 

As such the business case will be accompanied by a detailed design proposal, detailed cost plan 

To support this Stage and Plan of Works a Consultancy is required to provide Project Management and Cost Management Services.

The Stage of Work is planned to commence in February 2023. with a target completion of September/October 2023.

The duration of the contract is therefore 9 months, subject to the right of the Council (at its sole discretion) to exercise its right to extend the Contract by up to 3 months . The maximum length of the contract is therefore 12 months.

The recently approved Treasury Green Book 5 Case Outline Business Case codified a number of deliverables for the project, including:

Delivery of c.45 units of affordable housing comprised of a mix between general needs housing for older persons and self-contained accommodation for individuals with learning disabilities, including those 'in transition'
Delivery of affordable housing to meet the Council's requirement to increase supply of new-build accommodation.
Create a long-term source of revenue for the Council
Regeneration of a vacant and underutilised Council asset to help deliver the Council's priorities as set out in the Corporate Plan (2019-2023)
Create an opportunity to unlock existing sheltered housing stock identified for priority action for improvement or redevelopment
Provide a model for new specialist and supported housing that integrates the Council's ambitions to integrate technology into care.
Enhancements to the streetscape, public realm and placemaking on the site

A Budget has been approved by the Council to progress the scheme to the next stage, including:

taking the design to RIBA Stage 2-3 leading to a developed design, detailed cost plan, procurement strategy and planning application.
The production of a Green Book 5 Case Treasury Green Book Detailed Business Case to obtain gateway approval to submit the planning application, proceed to RIBA 4 and any additional resourcing required.
 This opportunity has been distributed on adamprocure.co.uk
